Pros:
- the receptionists really do try to take down all the information they can in order to get you the correct help.
- appointment times generally are not too far in advance
- most the time, there is a generally positive outcome with care

Cons:
- some of the receptionists sound so unhappy or just have a general “sick of this” attitude. On the phone. Often trying to rush you or huffing on the phone when you give a reason for the call. - a couple appointments I’ve received have been 3 weeks away and get cancelled last minute. I recently have been getting investigated for heart issues and part of that was getting an ECG. Which means another 3 weeks of waiting.
- in relation to having my heart investigated, I am quite young (23F) and I am often told that I “don’t need” something checked as I’m so young I shouldn’t have any issues. Despite having multiple BP readings of 140/90+ and being generally healthy in my lifestyle. It often gets left alone and I’m left to worry if I maybe hospitalised again.

So to summarise, some of the receptionists are lovely, some aren’t. It’s questionable whether you’ll have to wait a while for your appointment and whether you’ll have a good outcome. Overall, they’re okay to be with for your healthcare, but could definitely do with some improvements.
